sources.title: WAM-Nav: Asymmetric Latent World-Action Modeling for Unified Visual Navigation

omissions: Text extraction does not reconstruct figure images; inspect the retained PDF for figures and equation/table layout.
Separate supplemental material availability has not been fully verified.
The extraction-only visual limitation was addressed by inspecting the retained PDF: all figures and tables were visually read, and six final crops were inspected.

Identity: the inspected title page identifies arXiv:2606.04907v2 [cs.RO], 13 June 2026. Title and all twelve authors match the catalog after name-order normalization. The catalog does not specify a revision; v1 and revision differences were not supplied or compared (e01).
All five supplied text chunks were read individually. Reference pages 9–11 were read as text; visual inspection covered pages 1–8 and 12–19.
No code, external linked resources, or separate supplements were inspected; no experiments were reproduced.

synopsis: WAM-Nav jointly generates navigation trajectories and short-horizon visual latents using one shared Diffusion Transformer. Goal-conditioned visual and motion histories guide a 24-step action horizon with one future visual state. Reported zero-shot navigation improves over NavDP, but task balancing sacrifices specialized peaks, and physical failures expose camera visibility and body-clearance limits. Method, results and boundaries are traced in e02–e18.

problem.text: The authors target mapless Image-Goal, Point-Goal and No-Goal navigation. Their concern is that reactive policies lack explicit future perception, while sequential imagination–policy pipelines add latency and error. The proposed alternative couples action and visual prediction inside generation; learned geometric consistency is a motivation, not a formal collision-avoidance guarantee.

contributions.text: A shared generative backbone couples long action trajectories with short visual foresight, avoiding a separate inverse-dynamics action-extraction stage.
Two goal queries modulate visual memory and relative motion history before fusion into a compact context; one policy accommodates all three goal settings.

inputs: Recent visual observations; RGB is explicitly encoded, while the architecture caption and deployment describe RGB-D (e02, e17).
Action-accumulated planar pose history and an image, relative-coordinate, or masked no-goal condition (e02, e05).
outputs: A future action trajectory and Stable Diffusion VAE visual latents, jointly generated (e04).
Physical velocity commands are produced downstream by MPC trajectory tracking (e17).

steps.name: Preserve goal modality
steps.detail: A scratch-trained image ViT, sinusoidal coordinate encoding, or masked zero-state produces a base goal embedding. Separate learned projections produce visual-semantic query g_V and geometric query g_G.

steps.name: Retrieve visual and kinematic context
steps.detail: Frozen DINOv2 encodes visual patches. Sigmoid goal relevance adds a patchwise residual, reinforcing rather than deleting tokens. Executed actions update a pose buffer; positions are recentered and rotated into the current egocentric frame, with wrapped heading differences and front zero-padding.

steps.name: Let motion guide visual retrieval
steps.detail: A causal Transformer encodes relative motion. The geometric goal cross-attends to it to form o_kin; its projection biases learned queries that retrieve the goal-modulated visual memory through a Transformer decoder, producing context C.

steps.name: Denoise both prediction streams together
steps.detail: Action and VAE-latent tokens share self-attention at every DiT layer, with separate timestep modulation branches and shared cross-attention/FFN weights. Both attend to C. Defaults use eight history steps, 64 conditioning tokens, 16 DiT layers and horizons H_act=24, H_vis=1.

training.text: Training uses VLN-N1: over 400 simulated hours and 200K trajectories from six scene-asset families with domain randomization. Reported cost is approximately 8 × 120 GPU-hours. DINOv2 ViT-S/14 and the Stable Diffusion VAE remain frozen; the goal image encoder, fusion decoder, motion encoder and DiT train from scratch.

AdamW uses batch 256, peak learning rate 1.5 × 10^-4, weight decay 10^-4, cosine decay and 5% warmup. Joint flow-velocity regression is weighted with a symmetric InfoNCE goal-alignment term; visual and alignment weights are 0.25 and 0.1.

inference.text: At each receding-horizon decision, rebuild C and jointly integrate action and latent noise with ten Euler steps. The policy samples sixteen trajectories and executes the first sampled trajectory; the supplied method does not describe foresight-based ranking of candidates.

Physical deployment uses a Unitree G1, D455 RGB-D camera at 30 Hz and 20° downward pitch, and an onboard RTX 4060. Policy inference is configured at 1 Hz with approximately 1.3 GB GPU memory. MPC tracks predicted trajectories and generates motor velocity commands.

equations.explanation: V is visual memory, g_V the visual goal query, D the embedding dimension, and sigma the sigmoid. The residual preserves each patch while boosting goal-relevant features.
Flow time tau runs from Gaussian action/latent noise A_0,Z_0 to data A_1,Z_1. Target velocities are u_A=A_1-A_0 and u_Z=Z_1-Z_0.

Predicted velocities are jointly regressed; L_align is symmetric contrastive InfoNCE for equivalent goals. The two lambda coefficients weight visual regression and goal alignment. The expectation averages uniform flow time tau in [0,1] and Gaussian initial states.

results.setting: Zero-shot IsaacSim Dingo evaluation on ClutterScenes and InternScenes; original pretrained weights, no finetuning. Section 4.1 specifies 100 episodes per scene, 6,000 total.
results.metric: Success rate (SR) / success weighted by path length (SPL), percent; higher is better
results.interpretation: The SR gain is 6.8 percentage points, approximately 15.7% relative (reader calculation). For the Ours/NavDP Image-Goal SR and SPL entries, equal means of the four displayed scene categories agree with the printed averages after rounding. This does not establish the aggregation rule for every Table 3 cell or justify relabeling these summaries as pooled episode rates.

results.setting: Same zero-shot Dingo benchmark and four-category Table 3 summary.
results.interpretation: SR improves 2.6 percentage points, approximately 3.3% relative (reader calculation).

results.setting: Same benchmark; time capped at 120 seconds with early termination when locally stuck.
results.metric: Explored area (m²) / episode time (s), higher is better
results.interpretation: These measure coverage and episode persistence, not goal-reaching success. Reader calculation: NavDP’s four displayed area values (315.6, 274.1, 34.1, 43.9) average to 166.925 m², approximately 166.9, whereas the table prints 167.2. The reported value is retained; the source does not explain this discrepancy or provide an aggregation rule that resolves it.

results.value: Neither component: 42.1; latent only: 45.7; motion only: 43.9; both: 50.2. With H_act=24, H_vis=1/4/8/24 gives 50.2/46.2/39.6/30.4.
results.interpretation: Consistent with useful coupling and short foresight; missing repeat variability and compute-matched controls limit causal attribution.

results.setting: Table 1 per-decision comparison; timing hardware/profiling protocol unspecified.
results.interpretation: Lower arithmetic cost does not make WAM-Nav faster than NavDP; reported policy latency differs from configured deployment frequency.

results.setting: G1 in meeting room, warehouse, lobby and parking lot; ten trials per scene; goal modality not specified.
results.interpretation: A small physical execution study, distinct from simulated G1/H2 transfer in Table 8. No uncertainty interval is supplied.

limitations.text: Camera height and field of view can hide low nearby obstacles; camera-clear paths can still collide with the robot body because embodiment is not explicitly modeled.

Goal balancing is a tradeoff: visual-only queries reach 55.6% Image-Goal SR versus 50.2 jointly; geometric-only reaches 83.5% Point-Goal SR versus 80.4 jointly. The joint variant leads No-Goal coverage, not every task-specific maximum.

Table 9 lists NavDP SPL above SR in its Medium and Hard subsets; its Average columns are not explained by the displayed subset means. Absolute SR gaps also do not grow monotonically with difficulty. These entries need clarification before adopting the authors’ difficulty trend.

Pretrained baselines share an evaluation environment, not a controlled training budget. Qualitative decoded foresight examples do not quantify dynamics accuracy or establish physical safety guarantees.

reproduction.text: Reproduction needs the specified VLN-N1 data, frozen visual checkpoints, Table 2 architecture, and original baseline weights. The source omits training GPU model, total update count, exact success thresholds, simulator version and detailed InfoNCE pairing/temperature. RGB-D is named, but a depth-fusion pathway is not specified.

Deployment reports a 50 Hz control loop and 0.1-second command application without explaining their scheduling relationship. MPC parameters, action scaling and physical goal protocol also need clarification; Table 1 timing hardware cannot be inferred from the RTX 4060 deployment description.

Proposed checks: compare shared and attention-decoupled predictors under matched training budgets; repeat the visual-horizon sweep with per-horizon loss normalization and latency measurements. Both should use fixed evaluation episodes and repeated seeds.

reasoning.text: The recorded One Model × Joint prediction quadrant is supported by architecture: action and future-visual tokens share self-attention and generative parameters, rather than merely sharing a training dataset. Foresight participates in inference-time generation. Separate frozen encoders and downstream MPC do not imply separate world/policy generators. The latent-prediction subcategory fits VAE latents; no JEPA-specific objective is demonstrated.

discussionQuestions: Does inference-time cross-modal coupling improve navigation beyond the regularization supplied by the visual training loss (e06, e11)?
Would explicit body-clearance conditioning preserve transfer while reducing the failures in Appendix H (e18)?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title/author/affiliation block and arXiv margin
evidence.detail: WAM-Nav: Asymmetric Latent World-Action Modeling for Unified Visual Navigation; twelve named authors and seven affiliations; arXiv:2606.04907v2, 13 Jun 2026.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 3–4, Sections 3.1–3.2, Figure 2 and Eqs. (1)–(3)
evidence.detail: Modality-specific goal encoders form two queries. RGB patch memory receives sigmoid-weighted residual reinforcement. Figure 2 depicts a frozen vision encoder and shared generator; its caption describes RGB-D.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.2, Eqs. (4)–(5)
evidence.detail: The geometric goal queries causal motion features; the resulting kinematic token biases learned decoder queries over visual memory to form C.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 5–6, Sections 3.3–3.4, Eqs. (6)–(8)
evidence.detail: VAE future latents and actions share flow interpolation and DiT attention. The loss combines two velocity regressions and symmetric InfoNCE. Online control samples sixteen trajectories and selects the first.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 12–13, Appendix B, Algorithm 1 and Appendix C.1
evidence.detail: Action-accumulated poses use a sliding, front-zero-padded buffer, current-frame recentering/rotation and wrapped relative headings.

evidence.location: PDF p. 13, Appendix C.2 and Figure 5
evidence.detail: Separate adaLN-Zero branches feed shared action/image self-attention; both branches use context C with shared cross-attention and FFN weights.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Section 4.1, training/evaluation/metrics paragraphs
evidence.detail: VLN-N1 supplies over 400 hours and 200K trajectories. Cost is 8 × 120 GPU-hours. Evaluation uses 10 easy, 10 hard, 20 home and 20 commercial scenes, 100 episodes each; No-Goal time is capped at 120 seconds.

evidence.location: PDF p. 14, Table 2 and Appendix D
evidence.detail: Default history 8, action horizon 24, visual horizon 1, condition length 64, hidden dimension 384, sixteen DiT layers. Frozen DINOv2/VAE, scratch-trained remaining named modules, AdamW and ten Euler steps are specified.

evidence.location: PDF p. 15, Table 3, all three task blocks, Ours/NavDP rows and Average columns
evidence.detail: Image-Goal: 50.2/48.2 versus 43.4/41.4; Point-Goal: 80.4/78.0 versus 77.8/74.8; No-Goal area/time: 171.1/75.6 versus 167.2/72.5.

evidence.location: PDF p. 15, Table 4, all component rows and scene-group columns
evidence.detail: Overall SR/SPL: neither 42.1/40.8, latent only 45.7/43.8, motion only 43.9/42.9, both 50.2/48.2. Motion-only InternScenes SR is 30.0 versus 33.2 without either.

evidence.location: PDF p. 16, Table 5 and Appendix F.3 discussion
evidence.detail: Memory 4/8/16 gives SR 46.6/50.2/44.9; removing goal injection gives 44.5; decoupled/partially shared/full DiT gives 45.9/47.5/50.2.

evidence.location: PDF p. 16, Table 6, all goal-query variants
evidence.detail: Visual-only Image-Goal SR is 55.6; geometric-only Point-Goal SR is 83.5. Joint queries yield 50.2/80.4 respectively, and the largest No-Goal area/time, 171.1/75.6.

evidence.location: PDF p. 16, Table 7 and final Appendix F.3 paragraph
evidence.detail: At action horizon 24, visual horizons 1/4/8/24 yield SR 50.2/46.2/39.6/30.4 and SPL 48.2/43.8/37.3/28.1.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Table 1; p. 7, Q3 discussion
evidence.detail: Ours/NavDP/NWM latency is 0.26/0.16/1.43 seconds and TFLOPs 0.7/1.3/8.3. WAM-Nav has 234.9M total and 129.2M trainable parameters; table timing hardware is not identified.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Figure 4(a–b) and Section 4.2
evidence.detail: Physical G1 evaluation has ten trials in each of four scenes. Figure bars show Ours 8/9/10/7 successes and NavDP 4/6/7/2; text reports 85% average success.

evidence.location: PDF p. 17, Tables 8–9 and Appendix F.4
evidence.detail: Table 8 is IsaacSim Dingo/G1/H2 transfer. Table 9 gives NavDP Medium 33.8 SR/35.6 SPL and Hard 17.4/21.3; Ours Easy/Medium/Hard SR is 52.5/42.4/25.0, versus 46.2/33.8/17.4.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 17–18, Appendix G.1–G.2 and Figure 7
evidence.detail: G1 carries D455 and RTX 4060. Deployment uses 20° camera pitch, 30 Hz observations, 1 Hz inference, about 1.3 GB memory and MPC; it reports both 50 Hz control and 0.1-second command application.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Limitations; pp. 18–19, Appendix H and Figure 8
evidence.detail: Failures involve low obstacles missed near the camera and side-body collisions despite a passable camera trajectory.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Figure 3 and Q2 discussion
evidence.detail: Two qualitative scenes compare NavDP/WAM-Nav trajectories and GT/decoded latent foresight; visual fidelity and smoother avoidance are author interpretations of these examples.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 2–3, Introduction and Sections 2.1–2.2
evidence.detail: The authors motivate joint modeling through the latency/error costs of decoupled imagination and action pipelines and the limited anticipation of reactive navigation.

evidence.location: PDF p. 15, Table 3, Task 3: No-Goal Exploration, NavDP row, Easy/Hard/Home/Commercial M1 and Average M1 cells
evidence.detail: The four displayed NavDP explored-area entries are 315.6, 274.1, 34.1 and 43.9; the source prints 167.2 in the Average area cell. No aggregation formula or explanation of these entries is supplied.
